ruling.recommended_action: Escalate to RydeHELP human fare review: verify the meter distance against the partial GPS trace and the uncovered final 4 minutes, quantify the refundable metered distance for the 09:04–09:14 off-route segment, and issue the resulting voucher under NS-7. No account flag on the current profile.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a RydeTAXI metered journey (total $28.97 metered, distance $17.16 for 12.17 km), so detour kilometres feed directly into the fare and the RydeTAXI branch of RD-2 governs any refund; the refund base is the fare record's distance fare ÷ distance km, $17.16 ÷ 12.17 km = $1.4100/km [F7][RD-2]. On the merits of the one recorded deviation, the segment 09:04–09:14 drove 5.23 km against 1.08 km optimal, adding 4.15 km and reaching 1989 m from the optimal route; it is an unexplained deviation from the shortest and most direct route and is refundable under RD-1/RD-2 [F4][RD-1].

That segment is not excused by any branch: no traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window, and the only speed records are band 3 (20–29 km/h) on EU TONG SEN STREET and SENTOSA GATEWAY, not the band 1–2 the policy needs, so RD-4 exempts nothing [F14][F12][F13][RD-4]. The chat record is complete and fully timestamped with only the rider's 08:47 pickup note and the driver's 08:48 reply, so no rider message before the segment's 09:04 start agrees to any reroute; the driver's post-trip assertion that the GPS rerouted him is a claim and not rider consent [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5].

The money cannot be settled on this record. RD-2 refunds only the extra kilometrage attributable to an unexempted segment, i.e. the segment's extra_km × this trip's per-km rate = 4.15 km × $1.4100/km = $5.8515, ≈ $5.85 [F4][F7][RD-2] — not the billed excess of $7.04 (4.99 km × $1.4100/km) and not the whole 10.2 km vs 7.2 km difference of +3.0 km, which is not attributed to any off-route segment [F2][F5][RD-2]. If the trace's distance arithmetic is instead the correct measure the figure is $7.04 [F5][F7][RD-2], and the meter fares in F7 (12.17 km billed, $17.16 distance) are not internally consistent with the 10.2 km actual distance in F2, so the two candidate amounts differ and the record does not settle which one the meter actually billed.

On top of that, the GPS trace's last sample is 4 minutes before the 09:20:45 drop-off, so the tail of the trip is unmeasured and its mile-age cannot be attributed to either side [F1][RD-1]. Because the trace marks the GPS coverage as a fail and the record cannot fix the refundable amount, the case goes to a human reviewer; nothing about the driver's or rider's profile decides it [F16][F17].

Safety screen: I read all chat messages, the driver's statement and the complaint. The messages are an ordinary pickup exchange ("waiting outside Beach Station, with a black backpack"; "On my way, about 8 min, silver Toyota Altis") and the driver's statement is a factual assertion about the fare, with no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. No escalation ground on safety.
ruling.escalation_reason: evidence insufficient: The GPS trace ends 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off, so the final stretch of the route is unmeasured and its mileage cannot be attributed to any segment or to either party; the uncovered stretch cannot be measured, and the record therefore does not settle the refundable metered distance (F1, F4, F5, F7).

segment_findings.reason: Off-route segment 09:04–09:14 drove 5.23 km against 1.08 km optimal (+4.15 km, up to 1989 m off the optimal route) [F4]. The complete timestamped chat contains no rider message before 09:04 about the route — only the rider's 08:47 pickup note and the driver's 08:48 reply — so no consent exists for this segment, and the driver's post-trip 'the GPS rerouted me' statement is a claim, not rider consent (G11) [F8][F9][F10][F11][RD-5]. RD-4 does not excuse it: no incident near the route and only band-3 speeds on EU TONG SEN STREET / SENTOSA GATEWAY [F14][F12][F13][RD-4]. The segment is refundable under RD-2 [RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that the refundable amount is the billed excess of $7.04 (4.99 km × $1.4100/km) is not the RD-2 measure: RD-2 refunds extra_km of the unexempted segment only, 4.15 km × $1.4100/km = $5.8515 ≈ $5.85, and the billed excess is not attributed to any off-route segment [F4][F5][F7][RD-2].

The assertion that the untraced final 4 minutes do not matter is wrong as to evidence: the GPS trace ends 4 min 0 s before the 09:20:45 drop-off, so the tail mileage is unmeasured and the record does not settle the refundable amount; the case goes to a human [F1][F4][RD-1][RD-2].

The driver's profile shows 3 disputes in 90 days with 1 upheld but 0 route disputes upheld, so a prior upheld route deviation does not exist and RD-6's repeated-violation flag is unavailable [F17][RD-6].

The claim that the segment-matched figure is 'the most' that can be ordered back assumes the 4.15 km segment figure is the correct measure, but the meter's billed distance/fare (12.17 km, $17.16) and the 10.2 km actual distance conflict, so the amount is not settled on this record; the record also has an unmeasured tail [F2][F5][F7][F1][RD-2].

The claim that the untraced tail shields the driver cuts both ways: the trace fail means the tail mileage cannot be attributed to either side, and the one measured segment (09:04–09:14, +4.15 km) still counts under RD-1/RD-5, so the case escalates rather than resolving in the driver's favour [F1][F4][F8][F9][RD-1][RD-5].

The claim that the driven distance is what the meter 'legitimately bills' does not survive RD-1/RD-2: unattributed excess kilometrage on an unexempted deviation is not legitimately billable, and the record does not settle the amount [F4][F7][RD-1][RD-2].

Accepted as far as it goes — no rider message before 09:04 consents to the reroute — but the driver's statement that the GPS rerouted him is not a traffic fact under RD-4 and does not exempt the segment [F8][F9][F11][F14][RD-5][RD-4].
